question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - \cos{\left(t \right)}, - \sin{\left(t \right)}, 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle 2 y, - 2 x, 0\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle 2 y, - 2 x, 0\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), - 2 \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), 0\rangle \\ & =\langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(- 2 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 2 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =- 2 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} - 2 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(-2\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 2 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(- 4 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =- 4 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle t^{2} - t, t^{3} - t^{2}, - t^{2} + t\rangle$ for $t\in [0,1).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle - 2 z, 0, - 3 y\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t^{2} - t,\quad y=t^{3} - t^{2},\quad z=- t^{2} + t
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - 2 z, 0, - 3 y\rangle \\ & =\langle - 2 \left(- t^{2} + t\right), 0, - 3 \left(t^{3} - t^{2}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 t^{2} - 2 t, 0, - 3 t^{3} + 3 t^{2}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(t^{2} - t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(t^{3} - t^{2}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- t^{2} + t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 t - 1, 3 t^{2} - 2 t, 1 - 2 t\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 2 t^{2} - 2 t, 0, - 3 t^{3} + 3 t^{2}\rangle\cdot \langle 2 t - 1, 3 t^{2} - 2 t, 1 - 2 t\rangle \\ & =\left(2 t^{2} - 2 t\right)\cdot \left(2 t - 1\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2} - 2 t\right)+\left(- 3 t^{3} + 3 t^{2}\right)\cdot \left(1 - 2 t\right) \\ & =\left(4 t^{3} - 6 t^{2} + 2 t\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(6 t^{4} - 9 t^{3} + 3 t^{2}\right) \\ & =6 t^{4} - 5 t^{3} - 3 t^{2} + 2 t \\ & =6 t^{4} - 5 t^{3} - 3 t^{2} + 2 t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{1} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{1}\left(6 t^{4} - 5 t^{3} - 3 t^{2} + 2 t\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- \frac{5 t^{4}}{4}\right) + \left(- t^{3}\right) + \left(t^{2}\right) + \left(\frac{6 t^{5}}{5}\right)\right]_{0}^{1} \\ & =\left(\left(- \frac{5}{4}\right) + \left(-1\right) + \left(1\right) + \left(\frac{6}{5}\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right)\right) \\ & =- \frac{1}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle - 6 t^{3} + 6 t, 9 t^{2} + 9 t, t^{3} - t\rangle$ for $t\in [-1,0).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle - z, 0, - y\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 6 t^{3} + 6 t,\quad y=9 t^{2} + 9 t,\quad z=t^{3} - t
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - z, 0, - y\rangle \\ & =\langle - \left(t^{3} - t\right), 0, - \left(9 t^{2} + 9 t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - t^{3} + t, 0, - 9 t^{2} - 9 t\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 6 t^{3} + 6 t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(9 t^{2} + 9 t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(t^{3} - t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 6 - 18 t^{2}, 18 t + 9, 3 t^{2} - 1\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - t^{3} + t, 0, - 9 t^{2} - 9 t\rangle\cdot \langle 6 - 18 t^{2}, 18 t + 9, 3 t^{2} - 1\rangle \\ & =\left(- t^{3} + t\right)\cdot \left(6 - 18 t^{2}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(18 t + 9\right)+\left(- 9 t^{2} - 9 t\right)\cdot \left(3 t^{2} - 1\right) \\ & =\left(18 t^{5} - 24 t^{3} + 6 t\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(- 27 t^{4} - 27 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 9 t\right) \\ & =18 t^{5} - 27 t^{4} - 51 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 15 t \\ & =18 t^{5} - 27 t^{4} - 51 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 15 t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{-1}^{0} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{-1}^{0}\left(18 t^{5} - 27 t^{4} - 51 t^{3} + 9 t^{2} + 15 t\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- \frac{51 t^{4}}{4}\right) + \left(- \frac{27 t^{5}}{5}\right) + \left(3 t^{3}\right) + \left(\frac{15 t^{2}}{2}\right) + \left(3 t^{6}\right)\right]_{-1}^{0} \\ & =\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(- \frac{51}{4}\right) + \left(\frac{27}{5}\right) + \left(-3\right) + \left(\frac{15}{2}\right) + \left(3\right)\right) \\ & =- \frac{3}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle \cos{\left(t \right)}, - \sin{\left(t \right)}, \sin{\left(t \right)} - 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle - y + z, x - z, - x + y\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=\sin{\left(t \right)} - 1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - y + z, x - z, - x + y\rangle \\ & =\langle - \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - 1\right), \left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right) - \left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - 1\right), - \left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 1, - \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)} + 1, - \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - 1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 1, - \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)} + 1, - \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle\cdot \langle - \sin{\left(t \right)}, - \cos{\left(t \right)}, \cos{\left(t \right)}\rangle \\ & =\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 1\right)\cdot \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)} + 1\right)\cdot \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(- 2 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ & =- 2 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)} - 2 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)} \\ & =\sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- 2 t\right) + \left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(- 4 \pi\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(-1\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(-1\right)\right) \\ & =- 4 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

$$
x=- 3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad y=3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad z=\cos{\left(\pi t \right)}
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - y, 0, - x\rangle \\ & =\langle - \left(3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right), 0, - \left(- 3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, 0, 3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(\cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, 3 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}, - \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, 0, 3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle\cdot \langle 3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, 3 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}, - \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle \\ & =\left(- 3 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(3 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(3 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(- 9 \pi \sin^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(- 3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right) \\ & =- 9 \pi \sin^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)} - 3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)} \\ & =- 3 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)} + \frac{9 \pi \cos{\left(2 \pi t \right)}}{2} - \frac{9 \pi}{2}\end{aligned}
